questions.question: Is the property located in a government-authorized area and built as per the approved plan?
questions.description:
🏛️ Property Compliance Status
This determines which lenders (banks vs NBFCs) can process the loan application.
📋 What this means:
  • Fully compliant — Property is in an authorized area AND built as per the government-approved map/plan
  • Authorized but deviates from plan — Property is in an authorized area but the construction deviates from the approved plan/map
  • Not authorized — Property is NOT in a government-authorized area
💡 Tip: Not fully compliant does not mean the loan is rejected — some NBFCs fund non-authorized or deviated properties at different terms.

options.label: Yes — authorized area, as per approved plan
Authorized area, but not as per plan

condition.then: Properties that are not fully compliant may still be eligible for funding through select NBFCs. Fewer lenders will appear in the results, but options are available.

questions.question: How old is this property?
questions.description:
🏠 Property Age
The age of the property affects loan eligibility, maximum tenure, and valuation.
Why this matters:
  • Older properties may have lower loan-to-value ratios
  • Banks assess residual life — typically 60–75 years for RCC buildings
  • Properties over 25–30 years may face reduced tenure or rejection
  • For Flat/Floor: age of the building matters
  • For House/Villa: age of the main structure matters
💡 Tip: Check your property registration deed or builder's completion certificate for the exact year of construction.

questions.question: What is the carpet area of the property? (in sq ft)
questions.description:
📐 Carpet Area
Carpet area is the actual usable floor area within the walls — this is the primary metric banks use for property valuation.
How to find this:
  • Check your sale deed or agreement for recorded carpet area
  • For RERA-registered properties, carpet area is mentioned on the RERA portal
  • Your builder's allotment letter will have this detail
💡 Note: Don't confuse with built-up area (includes walls) or super built-up area (includes common areas). Banks value based on carpet area.

condition.then: Carpet area seems too low. Please enter the area in square feet.

questions.question: Has the building received its Occupancy Certificate (OC) / Completion Certificate (CC)?
questions.description:
📋 OC / CC Status
The Occupancy Certificate (OC) confirms the building is safe for occupancy. The Completion Certificate (CC) confirms construction was completed as per the sanctioned plan.
Why this is important:
  • Most banks require OC/CC for balance transfer and top-up processing
  • Without OC, lenders may consider the property as legally incomplete
  • Older buildings in municipal areas may have CC but not OC — that's common and usually acceptable
💡 Tip: Check with your housing society secretary or builder's office. For older municipal properties, the local municipal corporation can provide this.

questions.question: Was the house built with a sanctioned building plan from the local authority?
questions.description:
🏛️ Building Plan Approval
For independent houses and villas, lenders check whether the construction was done as per a plan sanctioned by the Municipal Corporation, Nagar Nigam, Gram Panchayat, or Development Authority.
Why this matters:
  • Sanctioned plan confirms the construction is legal and authorised
  • Unauthorised constructions may face lower LTV or rejection
  • Deviation from sanctioned plan may reduce property valuation
💡 Tip: The sanctioned plan / building permission document is usually with your property papers. If the house was built by a previous owner, check with the local municipal body.

Knowing your current rate type is important because it affects foreclosure charges when you transfer.

questions.question: How many EMI bounces have occurred in the last 12 months?
questions.description:
⚠️ EMI Repayment Track Record
Banks carefully review your EMI repayment history before approving a balance transfer. A clean track record significantly improves chances.
Typical Bank Requirements:
  • 0 bounces — Ideal, best rates and fastest processing
  • 1 bounce — Usually acceptable with explanation
  • 2+ bounces — Many banks may decline; limited options available
💡 Tip: A bounce means the EMI auto-debit failed due to insufficient funds. Even if you paid manually later, it counts as a bounce.

questions.question: What is the outstanding principal of the current home loan, as on today?
questions.description:
💳 Outstanding Principal
The outstanding principal is the remaining portion of your original loan amount that you still owe to the lender.
✅ Outstanding PrincipalRemaining original loan amount
❌ Not the same asTotal of remaining EMIs
📋 Where to Find This:
  • Check your "Schedule of Repayment" document
  • Log into your bank's net banking or app
  • Request a loan statement from your lender
  • Call your bank's customer service
💡 Remember: Each EMI you pay reduces this principal amount. The outstanding principal is always less than the total of remaining EMIs because EMIs include interest.

questions.question: Please specify the required Top-up amount ?
questions.description:
💰 Top-up Amount
Enter the additional amount you wish to borrow on top of your existing home loan.
📊 Top-up Calculation Factors:
  • LTV (Loan-to-Value) - Maximum lending percentage of property value
  • Property Value - Current market value of your property
  • Existing Loan - Outstanding balance of current home loan
💡 Formula: Maximum Top-up = (Property Value x LTV%) - Outstanding Loan Amount
⚠️ Note: Actual top-up amount may vary based on each lender's terms, your income eligibility, and credit score.

Lenders need to know the end use of top-up funds. Some purposes may attract different interest rates.

  • Debt Consolidation — Smart way to replace high-interest loans
